body:
Canadian alternative asset manager Sagard is entering the US wealth market, expanding its private credit footprint.

The expansion builds on Sagard’s strategic partnership with financial services group Baird, which includes collaboration on distribution, product innovation and advisor engagement in the US wealth segment.

Registered US advisors and accredited investors will now be able to access Sagard’s $5.9bn (£4.4bn) private credit platform.

“Sagard’s entry into the US wealth market represents an important step in the continued growth of our private credit platform,” said Dayna Kleinman, managing director and head of US wealth at Sagard. “Financial advisors are looking for experienced investment partners, clear education and thoughtful support as private markets become a more meaningful part of client portfolios. Our goal is to bring those capabilities together and help advisors engage with the asset class more confidently.”

As part of broadening investors’ access to private credit, Sagard will develop educational content, private markets insights, and other resources to help financial professionals evaluate the role of private credit in client portfolios.

The firm said it maintains a highly selective approach to middle-market lending in North America, focusing on companies with EBITDA ranging from approximately $10m to $100m.

The team specialises in lending to non-sponsored businesses, which are not owned or controlled by private equity firms. The firm also highlighted that it has no exposure to software companies, and the strategy does not rely on payment-in-kind interest to generate its current income.

“Our approach begins with understanding the business, its ability to repay and the protections available to lenders before we invest,” said Dev Gopalan, partner and portfolio manager at Sagard. “The breadth of opportunities we review allows us to remain highly selective and focus on businesses and structures that meet our investment standards.”

Sagard manages approximately $47bn in assets across 25 strategies, serving more than 550 LPs.
